title: Async weight streaming resume to eliminate first-token pause under cold starts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Multiple customer escalations in the past 48 hours reported intermittent first-token pauses (TTFT spikes) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private clusters for large-context model variants. Root cause analysis identifies a synchronous weight page-in and per-shard loader stall that blocks token generation threads during cold-start or rare worker eviction/resume paths. Impact: median TTFT for affected requests increased from ~60ms to ~420ms for cold sessions; tokens/sec dropped by 30%-60% during the stall window. Affected customers include two enterprise Dedicated tenants and multiple Hosted customers with on-demand model fanout.

Root cause: when a worker is resuming a model instance (eviction recovery or initial placement), the weight loader blocks on per-shard read+decompress on the fast path. This interacts poorly with our multiplexed request queue and kernel preemption heuristics: while the loader holds the worker, incoming requests wait for token generation threads, producing first-byte latency spikes and downstream queuing that reduces overall tokens/sec throughput. The synchronous path was introduced as part of a prior reliability patch that simplified error handling but neglected non-blocking resume.

Proposed immediate fix (hotfix): implement asynchronous weight streaming with resume hooks: move disk read + decompression into an async background streamer that publishes ready segments and triggers a non-blocking handoff to the inference threads. Provide a lightweight in-memory readiness bitmap so generation can begin on primed shards while lower-priority shards finish streaming. Add a circuit-breaker to fall back to current synchronous behavior if streamer cannot keep up.

Rollout plan: 1) Land minimal streamer with feature flag and an opt-in config per deployment (hosted/dedicated/private). 2) Canary on a small Dedicated pool and Hosted region with low-risk traffic (2026-03-12 22:00 UTC), monitor TTFT, tokens/sec, OOMs, and kernel preemptions. 3) Expand to 25% of traffic after 1h if metrics stable, 75% after 6h, full rollout next day. For Private customers require opt-in by default and provide migration playbook.

Verification: create a dashboard comparing median and p95 TTFT (cold vs warm sessions), tokens/sec per worker, and worker resume latency. Target: reduce median cold TTFT for affected models from 420ms -> <=120ms and remove the multi-second tail.

Fallbacks and mitigations: if regressions appear (OOMs or throughput degradation), toggle the streamer feature flag and enable a prioritization config that prefetches small prefix shards first. Also prepare a small scheduler patch to temporarily deprioritize weight loads during high request-pressure windows.

Artifacts and links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/Async+Weight+Streaming+Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7891 Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttft/async-weight-streaming-canary Incident notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-10-weight-resume-pauses

Longer term: evaluate on-disk compressed memory mapping and persistent shared memory pools for models with high churn. Consider integrating quantized shard-on-demand support to reduce streaming size.
